subject: EU exclusion-zone: operator escrow, SCCs, and evidence for in-region processing
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Schmidt <anna.schmidt@novamed.com>, legal@novamed.com
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, irene.choi@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-01T09:14:00Z
Subject: EU exclusion-zone: operator escrow, SCCs, and evidence for in-region processing

Hi Anna / Novamed legal team,

Thanks again for the conversation yesterday. Per our follow-up, I wanted to capture what Redwood can commit to for an "EU exclusion-zone" deployment and the kinds of artifacts you asked for so we have alignment before we prepare formal responses. High level: you asked for contractual commitments (SCCs + supplementary measures), operational evidence of in-region inference only (no operator access outside EU), and proof of deletion / backup handling.

What we can provide today (short summary):
- SCCs: We will execute the EU SCCs (2021 standard) with Novamed. We can include bespoke Special Conditions around operator access and subprocessor notifications in the DPA exhibit.
- Technical isolation: Private VPC deployment in our EU region (Frankfurt or Dublin). Control plane endpoints can be restricted to Novamed IPs.
- Operator access escrow & affidavit: We can produce an operator-access affidavit signed by our Head of Security describing the precise circumstances under which operator/engineer access is permitted (P0 incident, customer-requested debug) and the controls in place (time-limited access, session recording, MFA). We can also discuss a third-party escrow arrangement for a signed operator-affidavit to be held with an independent notary if that helps your risk team.
- KMS and keys: Option to use Novamed-managed KMS (bring-your-own-key) with HSM-backed keys in the EU. Redwood will only have wrapped-key material and cannot decrypt without a customer-initiated key unwrap.
- Backups & deletion: We will provide deletion runbooks, timestamps for logical deletion, and retention windows for backups. For backups, our standard safe-restore window is 30 days; we can negotiate a stricter SLA and provide deletion attestations (log-based evidence) and guidance on secure backup destruction.

Attached is a short technical answers PDF that maps these capabilities to the items on your checklist.

To keep this moving, could you confirm: 1) which EU region you prefer (FRA / DUB), 2) whether escrowed operator-affidavit + signed notary is required or if an internal affidavit + auditable logs suffice, and 3) the level of backup retention you need (30 / 14 / 0 days for restore windows)?

If helpful, we can schedule a 30-min technical + legal sync with our security and privacy leads later this week.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Head of Product Security
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-eu-sccs-technical-answers.pdf (2 pages, Q&A)

From: Anna Schmidt <anna.schmidt@novamed.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, irene.choi@redwood.ai
Cc: legal@novamed.com
Date: 2027-05-01T11:03:00Z
Subject: Re: EU exclusion-zone: operator escrow, SCCs, and evidence for in-region processing

Thanks Mina — helpful summary. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Region: FRA preferred, DUB is acceptable but FRA is our default.
2) Operator affidavit: Our DPO team would prefer escrowed third-party-signed operator affidavits (not just internal statements) because the current audit path requires an independently verifiable signature.
3) Backups: We need a maximum restore window of 14 days and documented proof of permanent destruction for backups older than retention. Where possible we require a retention-proof digest (logs + hash) showing deletion event.
4) Subprocessors: Please provide the current subprocessor list for the FRA region and the contract rank (who has access to KMS wrapped keys).

We also have a Novamed internal SCCs checklist attached so you can map items to our risk categories. Can your legal team draft the DPA exhibit language for operator access restrictions and an annex describing the escrow process? Once we have the draft we will share with procurement.

Anna
Anna Schmidt
Head of Compliance & Privacy
Novamed

Attachments: novamed-sccs-checklist.xlsx

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, irene.choi@redwood.ai, jordan.blake@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-02T08:22:00Z
Subject: Fwd: EU exclusion-zone: operator escrow, SCCs, and evidence for in-region processing

Folks — forwarding Novamed's replies and checklist. Key asks they flagged: FRA region, third-party-escrowed operator affidavit, 14-day backup restore window with deletion-proof hashes, and subprocessor exposure for FRA deployments.

Quick notes on internal owners:
- Legal (Lauren): draft DPA exhibit language + escrow wording.
- Security/Privacy (Irene): confirm feasibility of third-party-notarized affidavit and define the operator access gating (what qualifies as P0 incident, logs retained).
- Product Ops (Jordan): confirm whether FRA deployment currently uses any cross-region failover or operator tooling that would cause EU egress; if so, outline mitigation (route-only-inregion, region affinity).

I attached an operator-affidavit template that we can populate. We should aim to deliver a DPA-exhibit + affidavit draft by EOD Monday so Novamed can review.

Thanks — Mina

Attachments: operator-affidavit-template.docx

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, irene.choi@redwood.ai, jordan.blake@redwood.ai, anna.schmidt@novamed.com
Date: 2027-05-03T15:42:00Z
Subject: Re: EU exclusion-zone: operator escrow, SCCs, and evidence for in-region processing

Anna / team — looping in Novamed as promised. Short plan from legal:

1) DPA exhibit: We will draft explicit operator-access restrictions and an escrow paragraph that explains the notary-held affidavit process (who signs, how often it's refreshed — propose annual renewal). Expect first pass by COB Monday.
2) Subprocessor list: Jordan, please compile current FRA-region subprocessors and note any global control-plane services. We will mark those with potential access to wrapped key metadata.
3) Affidavit template: I will review the operator-affidavit-template.docx and produce a notarizable language block we can present to Novamed for escrow. We should also include a short attestation workflow: how Novamed can trigger an access review and how access logs are delivered.
4) Backup deletion proof: Ops should provide a sample deletion digest (log snippet + sha256 of deletion notification) so they can see the kind of evidence we will supply.

Anna — can you share the procurement timeline? If Novamed needs signed SCCs + DPA within two weeks we will prioritize. Otherwise target for legal + ops draft by Monday and a technical call mid-next week (30 minutes) to walk through the artifacts.

Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Contracts
Redwood Inference
